chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who hired a wet nurse and entrusted his child to her, then she disappeared with the child for years. Then she returned with the child, while his mother claimed that she did not recognize him, and her family claimed that they did not recognize him. He عليه السلام said: “They have no right to do that; they must accept him, for the wet nurse is trusted.”

key_terms.ظِئْرًا: a wet nurse hired to suckle and care for a child
key_terms.فَدَفَعَ إِلَيْهَا وَلَدَهُ: he entrusted his child to her care
key_terms.فَغَابَتْ بِالْوَلَدِ سِنِينَ: she was absent with the child for years
key_terms.مَأْمُونَةٌ: considered trusted and reliable in custody

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wet nurse returns a child after many years and the family claims not to recognize him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a hired wet nurse who returns with a child after a long absence. Imam Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام rules that the family must accept the child, because the wet nurse is regarded as a trusted custodian in this context. The narration reflects principles of trust, custody, and family recognition in fiqh.
